Then the Goddess, having been cursed by Vasiṣṭha, was never fruitful;
she was never pleased at any time except through the practice of the Cīna method.
Dhāriṇī spoke to that best of practitioners, who was difficult to perceive:
"Why do you treat me with such terrible anger?"
Janārdana, in the form of a Buddha, alone truly understands my practice of worship; no one else knows it in reality.
"This time has been spent by you in vain and with great exertion,
O one of contrary conduct and character, who do not know my true nature."
Since this [image] has now attained the presence of Viṣṇu, who possesses the form of Buddha,
therefore, O observer of noble vows, worship me through that very practice you have desired.
"At that very moment, O child, she becomes gracious toward you; of this there is no doubt.
Thus ends the first chapter in the Ācārasāra-tantra.
Śiva said:
Then that great sage Vasiṣṭha, desiring to understand the conduct and knowledge of the one who possesses the form of a Buddha, went to pay homage to the Goddess.
Then, having gone to the land of Mahācīna, that bull among sages beheld [the place] on the slope of the Himavat, frequented by the lords of practitioners.
66b) By means of a shameless posterior, endowed with beauty and youth,
with a mind intoxicated by wine, and with an overflowing display of amorous grace;
Clad in the attire of the erotic sentiment (*śṛṅgāra-rasa*) which enchants the world,
devoid of fear and shame, and intent upon meditation, [he beheld] the Goddess.
The Lord was surrounded by a thousand amorous women,
his eyes languid and reddened from the drinking of wine.
Beholding him from afar, Vasiṣṭha, perceiving him to be the very form of the Buddha,
was filled with wonder as he recalled the one who carries one across the ocean of worldly existence.
"What is this deed being performed by Viṣṇu in the form of a Buddha?
This practice, which contradicts the teachings of the Vedas, is in my view improper."
While the high-souled Vasiṣṭha was reflecting thus, a voice from the sky spoke clearly: "O you of noble vows, do not worry."
O Sage, that which is the supreme conduct for a practitioner who seeks liberation is this;
in the view of one whose conduct is contrary to this, she does not become pleased.
If you desire her favor before long,
then, O observer of noble vows, worship her according to this Chinese custom.
Hearing the voice from the sky, his body covered in horripilation,
Vasiṣṭha, exceedingly delighted, prostrated himself on the ground like a staff.
Then, O Pārvatī, having risen after a short while with palms joined in reverence, that sage went to the abode of Viṣṇu who was in the form of Buddha.
Then, not seeing him, being overwhelmed by the intoxication of wine, the old man, with a clear mind, said: "For what purpose have you come here?"
Then, having bowed to the Buddha, the great sage Nāśra spoke that which had been uttered by the goddess Tāriṇī for the purpose of his own worship.

Having heard this, the Blessed One, the Buddha, who consists of the knowledge of reality, spoke to Vasiṣṭha: "One who possesses that knowledge has the authority to engage in conduct free from conceptual thought."
O Sage, the conduct of Tāriṇī is always to be kept secret;
however, because of my devotion to you, it shall never be disclosed in this matter.
The Buddha said:
Now I shall describe the rules of conduct which bestow all prosperity upon the Goddess;
by the mere performance of which one sinks into the ocean of worldly existence.
It truly pacifies all sorrow, increases bliss,
consists of the knowledge of reality, and directly bestows the fruit of liberation.
67a) Mental purification such as ritual bathing is mental; mental recitation is supreme;
mental worship is divine; and mental libations and so forth are likewise mental.
Every moment is indeed auspicious; nowhere is there found an inauspicious time.
There is no distinction between day and night, nor between twilight, day, and night.
One should not perform purification of clothes, seats, beds, houses, marketplaces, or of touch and so forth with water; here, one should practice the mind free from conceptual construction.
In this [practice], there is no requirement for purity and the like, nor is there any defect such as impurity;
one should worship the Goddess in every way, whether unwashed or having already eaten.
At midnight, in a pure place, one should cause offerings to be presented with the bali-mantra; one must never harbor hatred toward women, especially during the great worship.
One must never, under any circumstances, engage in their censure, physical assault, deceit, or unkindness; otherwise, it will create an obstacle to success.
Women are gods; women are life; women alone are the ornament.
One must always behave toward the families of women as one would toward one's own wife, or otherwise [there will be ruin].
The supreme practitioner, girt with the garland born of the Mahācīna-krama, should offer that substance fashioned by his hand to Mahādevī.
If one recites the mantra at night, what could be difficult for him to attain?
There is no fruit that cannot be achieved when one is encircled by the Mahācīna-kramalatā.
O Keśava, even a sixteenth part of that [merit] does not equal the merit of entering a vine-cottage;
indeed, entering a vine-cottage yields a fruit greater than sitting upon a corpse.
Having come to the abode of Śāśāna, with hair disheveled and naked as the directions,
encircled by the great creeper of the Cīna-krama, one shall attain liberation.
Having placed a large conch shell at the place of recitation, one should perform the recitation while standing upright;
here there is no restriction regarding the directions, nor is there any restriction regarding sitting and so forth.
One should not observe fixed rules regarding time for recitation, nor for worship and the like, nor even for offerings;
it is taught that one may act according to one's own will, provided the mind remains focused on what is perceived.
Considering his purpose accomplished and feeling satisfied within his own mind,
he should worship with clusters of fragrant white and red *lauhitī* flowers.
With auspicious bilva and kuravaka flowers, excluding tulasī,
[one should worship] in a place with a single liṅga, in a cremation ground, in an empty house, or at a crossroads.
67b) Abiding there, the yogin should accomplish Tārā, the savior of the world;
likewise Tāriṇī, Dakṣiṇā, Kālī, Sundarī, and Bhairavī.
By means of the Mahācīna-krama, these are accomplished without a doubt;
here too, the method of the goddess Sundarī Bhairavī exists.
The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is the means of crossing over to accomplishment, but not at all without the *Cīna* method;
the practice of the *Mahācīna* method is supreme for the best of practitioners.
By reciting this Tāriṇī vidyā, one shall uplift ten million members of one's lineage;
his ancestors rejoice and sing songs of praise with joy.
He who is born in our family will be a knower of the lineage;
he is blessed, a master of family wisdom, a poet, and a scholar.
He is of noble birth, he is a man of virtuous deeds, he is a worthy practitioner;
he is a Brāhmaṇa, he is a knower of the Vedas, he is a maintainer of the sacred fire, and he is one who has been initiated.
He is a renunciant at the sacred seats of pilgrimage; he is free from desire, all-pervading, observant of vows, a drinker of the Soma, illustrious, and indeed Manu himself.
He is indeed remembered as a Vaiṣṇava, he is a Śaiva, and he is a Gāṇapatya,
who constantly worships Tāriṇī through the practices of the Mahācīna-krama.
Thus ends the second chapter in the Ācāra-tantra.
The illustrious Śiva said:
Having heard these words of Hari, who had assumed the body of a Buddha,
the sage Vasiṣṭha spoke to him again with his palms joined in reverence.
Vasiṣṭha said:
O Blessed One, Lord of the gods, O Lord consisting of the knowledge of reality,
the practice of the Mahācīna-krama has been described by you to me.
"O Supreme Lord, this [wine] alone is the primary thing, as is the woman;
tell me, which of these two is the more primary?"
The Blessed One said:
O Sage, in this supreme conduct, these two are indeed equal:
the preeminence of women and that of the gods; of this there is no doubt.
Since that auspicious Goddess is presided over by the Divine within the bodies of women,
therefore their preeminence is declared in all forms of worship.
Vasiṣṭha said:
"Speak, O Lord who knows the ordinances of the gods, you who consist of all-knowledge:
how it is that women have been made objects of worship by the best of practitioners."
The Blessed One said:
On the seat of the womb (yonipīṭha), the seat of mantra (maṃtrapīṭha), and the seat of the yantra (yaṃtrapīṭha),
Mahāmāyā, divided into three forms, is worshipped by the most excellent practitioners.
Among all the sacred seats (pīṭhas), the Yonipīṭha is the most preeminent;
when the Goddess is worshipped there, she becomes instantly propitious.
O Sage, the ritual of Yoni-pūjā is the supreme cause of the eight Siddhis beginning with Aṇimā; it is the complete means for accomplishing all my goals.
The river Kāpālinī, a courtesan, a washerwoman, a barber’s wife,
a Brāhmaṇa woman, a Śūdra girl, and likewise a cowherd’s daughter.
The prostitute of a garland-maker is proclaimed as one of the nine types of virgins; alternatively, she may be any woman among all living beings who is clever and endowed with auspicious marks.
Having brought the supreme, auspicious leader of these very [beings]—
Sundarī, intoxicated with youth, shameless, and sweetly smiling— [he approached].
Having made her naked and having anointed her with sandalwood, saffron, and perfumes, he then [placed] her with loose hair within the circle of her womb.
Having propitiated and worshipped the lineage of gurus and performed the six-limbed worship,
one should then perform the worship on the pedestal and worship Śivā in its center.
In that case, O Sage, there is no invocation nor the placement of seed-syllables;
rather, having worshipped with the ritual offerings and then again having offered the *arghya*, [one should proceed].
Having recited the mantra at the linga and having worshipped Maheśvara as Bhairava,
one should thereafter perform a fire sacrifice (homa) with perfumes, unbroken grains of rice, and flowers.

With the mind as the ladle, I perpetually offer the oblations of merit and demerit into the fire of the Self, which is kindled by those very offerings, through the path of the *suṣumṇā* and directed toward the senses.
O Sage, this sacrificial mantra ends with "svāhā" for each individual oblation;
O Sage, one should offer the final full oblation (pūrṇāhuti) at the conclusion of the recitation.
Supported by the two hands of the Apsaras Prakāśā, with the Unmanī as the sacrificial ladle,
I offer [the oblation] into the fire filled with the fuel of the fruits of dharma and adharma.
This mantra, ending with *svāhā*, bestows liberation from terrible sins;
one should never look upon the naked Śakti except at the time of worship.
Practitioners must never drink the nectar except at the time of worship;
for if they see it or drink it otherwise, their weapons perish and they fall into the state of a beast.
A Brahmin may drink liquor during the Sauśamanyā family rite;
having drunk it on any other occasion out of desire, a man must perform penance.
In ancient times, having heard from Bhārgava that the goddess Vāruṇī was truly present,
Brahmā, the manifest preceptor of the worlds, went into the presence of Bhārgava.
O Brahman, this worldly liquor is like the nectar of the gods, which is composed of the essence of tranquility and is equal to the nectar of the conduct of Brahma.
The Goddess, who consists of the knowledge of Brahman, is born through the Kula practice;
and at the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice, the Lord of the Gods is indeed gratified by the Surā liquor.
"O Brahmā, let this liquor be released from its curse by you";
then that son of Bhṛgu, having prostrated before Brahmā, spoke.
"O Grandfather, let my word not be in vain, and let your word also be unfailing;
for that purpose, I have undertaken this vow."
O Lord, listen with a focused mind as I proclaim the three mantras for the sake of liberation from the curse of liquor during the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice according to the family tradition.
The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle;
I shall destroy the sin of killing a Brahmin that has arisen from your mental projection.
O Goddess, born from the solar disc, born from the abode of Varuṇa,
consisting of the seed-syllable of Amā, may you be liberated from the curse of Śukra.
O Goddess, if the Praṇava is the seed-syllable of the gods and consists of the sacrifice to Brahman,
by that [recitation], may he expiate the sin of killing a Brahmin.
Having spoken thus and prostrated before Brahmā three times,
O Goddess, Bhārgava departed for his own abode, and Brahmā went to his own residence.
When a knower of Brahman, having drunk wine according to the family custom,
stumbles repeatedly and falls, the nine *yadīs* cling to his body.
For that duration of time, O Goddess, she is honored in the world;
having drunk again and again, and having drunk once more, she falls upon the surface of the earth.
Having risen and drunk again, rebirth is no longer found;
having drunk according to the *ali* and *kula* traditions, [one enjoys] a woman endowed with youth.
It destroys, in that very instant, the sins accumulated over ten million lifetimes;
by drinking it repeatedly and reciting the mantra, one is liberated along with ten million of one's kinsmen.
The goddess dwells in the world of Brahmā; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
There alone one attains liberation and is not born again on earth.
Having drunk it, one should worship the Goddess; one certainly attains lordship.
Therein alone one finds dissolution and never returns again.
Having drunk [it] and become an Agnihotrin, the practitioner becomes a vessel for the sovereignty of the three worlds;
he is born as an excellent one, possessing great enjoyments and great happiness.
Having drunk [the nectar] and having caused [the self] to eat, that yogi then becomes "I am the Haṃsa"; thereafter, he arises as a hero, liberated while living throughout the three worlds.
Long-lived and subject to old age, yet liberated from all sins,
he attained both strength and the state of perfection.
Thus has been told the equal [account] of how the naked goddess (Digaṃvarī) is to be worshipped;
by worshipping the goddess even once, one is liberated from all sins.

Having thus worshipped the Goddess, what is there in the three worlds that cannot be accomplished? Even when Hara is enraged, nothing remains unattainable once one has worshipped the sky-clad goddess.
The lords of the world are the agents of creation, maintenance, dissolution, and so forth;
by worshipping them through yogic practices within their terrible forms, one is liberated.
A sonless man obtains a son, and a poor man becomes wealthy,
by beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight until it reaches the fifteenth day.

Whoever worships the naked goddess (Digaṃvarī) every day for as many days as there are lunar dates (tithis), for him there shall be the attainment of mantra-siddhi; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
The rites of heroic accomplishment (*vīrasādhana*) are difficult to achieve;
however, out of affection for you, this perfectly equal method of accomplishment has been revealed.
This should be guarded with great effort and not shown even to one's own sons.
Thus has this unsurpassed ritual of worship been described to you.
69b) And in every way, one should thus conceal the means of accomplishment (sādhana), like a mother’s paramour.
Thus ends the third chapter in the Ācārasāra-tantra.
Vasiṣṭha said:
Tell me of the vessels resting upon the Kulas, the characteristics of the meats,
the preparation of the Kula substances, and their very majesty.
O treasure-house of compassion, I desire to hear all about the sin that arises from non-performance [of rites] and the fruit that arises from performance; please speak.
The Blessed One said:
O Sage, listen; I shall declare that which you ask of me.
By the mere remembrance of it, one attains equality with the gods.
Without a support (ādhāra), there is no stability, and the Mothers are not satisfied;
therefore, the leader of the lineage should prepare the support according to the prescribed rule.
Alternatively, one should construct a circular and beautiful enclosure made of gold,
silver, stone, tortoise shell, skull, conch, or clay.
O Sage, listen with a concentrated mind as I shall explain the family substances:
twelve *prasthas* of water and half a *prastha* of clarified butter.
One should place four prasthas of rice, two prasthas of milk,
and a handful of sprouts into a single jar.
One should place [the substance] in a cool, deity-consecrated location for two days;
then, having placed it upon the fire, one should cook it in a measure corresponding to its own size.
Having planted [the seed], the wise man should lead it to that supreme state;
then, having ground it with a *prastha* of milk, he should mix it together with both hands.
One should stir it with milk using a perfectly pure ladle;
this is renowned as Paiṣṭī, worshipped by gods and dānavas alike.
The evil-minded person who, in this world, performs [a rite] for the sake of his own interest rather than for the worship of the lineage,
goes to a terrible hell along with twenty-one generations of his family.
O Sage, having worshipped the gods and the ancestors according to the path prescribed in the scriptures,
one who drinks liquor and eats meat while remembering the Guru incurs no fault.
He who consumes liquor and other such substances for the sake of the pleasure of his vows is a sinner;
he who is free from personal desire may consume them for the propitiation of the deity.
Even an outcaste who possesses knowledge of the Kula excels the Brahmin;
whereas he who is a follower of the Kula but does not perceive nor revere the Kula-knowledge [is inferior].
Fie on his life in this world! Fie, fie on his manliness!
Those who perform meritorious deeds are worthy of veneration; they alone are true yogis.

Those in whose minds, by the power of fortune, the knowledge of the lineage shines forth— they are to be revered, they are great-souled ones, they have accomplished their purpose, and they are the best among men.
In the minds of those in whom the knowledge of the Kula has been generated,
I have previously terrified all beings by means of tens of millions of scriptures.
Those who pride themselves on knowing the ultimate truth do not understand the family dharma;
indeed, all the scriptures of the Paśus were spoken by me alone.
Through the *smṛtyuttara* and the *valamantra*, those great nooses employed by the evil-minded for the purpose of delusion arise according to their own desires.
For them, however, there is no happy rebirth even in hundreds of millions of eons;
many of their own people, having heard the Kaula Dharma, have become possessors of knowledge.
Thus, even a person of good intellect, being utterly deluded by the influence of others, censures [the teaching].
Vasiṣṭha said:
If human beings were to achieve success solely through the drinking of liquor,
then all those devoted to drinking would have attained perfection without even the need for effort.
If liberation for people in this world were to occur through sexual union with women,
then all living beings in the world would be liberated simply by consorting with women.
The elder said:
In this regard, hear the reply: the Great Abode (Mahālaya), which is the family dharma of my sons, bestows liberation upon all beings who practice this dharma.
That which is drunk in vain is called the drinking of *surā*;
it has been declared in the Vedas and other scriptures to be indeed a great transgression (*mahāpātaka*).
Vasiṣṭha said:
I wish to hear from your own lips, in particular, the dharma of my family;
for indeed, there is no one else who is your equal in knowing its specific details.
O Supreme Lord, O Compassionate One, if you have grace for me, please tell me of the majesty of that Dharma, which is the highest of all Dharmas.
The Blessed One said:
O Sage, listen; I shall proclaim that which you ask of me.
By the mere hearing of it, one will become dear to the yoginīs.
That which was previously told by me concerning Śiva, Brahmā, Guha, and others, I shall now tell you out of affection; listen with a one-pointed mind.
This great wonder, which has come down through a succession of lineages, is to be guarded by the mind;
though it is not to be told according to the ultimate truth, nevertheless I shall speak of it.
The Vedas are the most excellent of all; the Vaiṣṇava [scripture] is superior to the Vedas;
the Śaiva is superior to the Vaiṣṇava; and the Dakṣiṇa is the best of all, even superior to the Śaiva.
The Left (Vāma) is superior to the Right (Dakṣiṇa); the Siddhānta is superior to the Left;
the Kaula is superior to the Siddhānta; and there is indeed nothing higher than the Kaula.
O Goddess, having churned the great ocean of the Vedas and Agamas with the churning-stick of knowledge, this is the most secret of secrets, the essence of essences, and the supreme transcendence.
Your knowledge encompasses all phenomena; all phenomena have been extracted by you.
On one side are all dharmas: sacrifices, sacred fords, vows, and so forth.
O beloved, this family tradition is superior to all sacrifices;
just as nine hundred rivers enter into the ocean, so do they flow into it from every side.
In the same way, all commitments and all foundations are indeed contained within the family;
just as the footprints of all living beings are encompassed within the footprint of an elephant.
And all philosophical systems, O Sage, are likewise contained within this family alone;
just as all rivers are not equal to the river of the gods (the Gaṅgā).
In the same way, all vows are not equal by virtue of their respective family-dharmas,
just as there is a difference between Mount Meru and a mustard seed, or between the sun and a firefly.
Likewise, there is a great difference between this person and this family;
for if there were any man on earth as wise as I, he would be my equal.
In the same way, O best of sages, there exists throughout the three worlds a family dharma [attained] through many births, meditations, and austerities.
The wise attain liberation, for the Kaulikas are indeed liberated while living;
this is the truth, the truth, and again the truth—this is the absolute truth, without a doubt.
What is the use of speaking much here? Listen with focused attention;
there is no dharma equal to the Kaula—this I tell you as the truth.
If one is a yogi, he cannot be an enjoyer; if he is an enjoyer, he cannot possess yoga.
Therefore, this Kaula system, which consists of both yoga and enjoyment, is indeed superior to all.
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Ācārasāra Tantra.
The Blessed One said:
I shall proclaim the eight pledges; listen with one-pointed attention, O great sage, for by the mere knowledge of which the practitioner attains accomplishment.
One may cause [it] to be destroyed or protect it; one may censure it or not look upon it;
one may worship it and cultivate it, but one should avoid it and never feel disgust for it.
O beloved, one may indeed destroy desire, anger, envy, the transformation arising from the senses, sleep, shame, and dejection— this group of eight.
The mantra, the mudrā, and the rosary string originate from the Yoginīs and the Vīras;
one should keep all of this—the Bhairava Āgama and its practice—secret.
One should never, under any circumstances, disparage for a long time the deity, the guru, the gods, the sacred knowledge, the practitioner, women, or one's own auspicious and inauspicious karma.

One should not look upon a maiden, a woman with power, a beast at play, a naked woman with exposed breasts, gambling, strife, those seeking sinful ends, or one of noble lineage [in an improper manner].
One should worship the Guru, the Goddess, as well as the Sādhaka, Śakti, the Ātman, and the Avyaya;
one should also diligently worship all those who accomplish that Śakti.
One should always contemplate with true reality the instructions and teachings of the guru, the deities at the sacred fords given by the virtuous, one's own duty, and the traditions of one's family.
The seeker of accomplishment should avoid approaching those who are forbidden, the company of rogues, fickleness, falsehood, and sinful assemblies.
One should not feel disgust toward feces, urine, blood, moisture, the limbs of the low-born, flesh, wine, or even the carrying of a skull; these eight indeed are not to be loathed.
Thus, whatever object there may be in the three worlds that a practitioner does not obtain here by performing the conduct of the pledge (samayācāra), [it shall be attained].
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O cause of the dissolution of the universe! O Lord, how may perfection be attained through the Kula practice, O Maheśvara?
If drinking that wine and consorting with another’s wife were both acts of success resulting from the performance of unrighteousness, then, O Lord, resolve all my doubt.
71b) Śiva said:
"Excellent, O Goddess of gods! I have been well questioned; listen as I speak to you.
Formerly, in the beautiful Dāruvana forest, there were supreme sages who were practitioners."
They violate the wives of others and constantly consume liquor;
seeing that improper conduct, Brahmā approached him with meat.
O God of gods, Mahādeva, whose nature is creation, preservation, and dissolution,
may you protect those who are devoted to drinking liquor here in this forest of Aru.
They violate the wives of others and consume intoxicants, deluded;
they are naked and shaven-headed—how can there be any [auspicious] destiny for them?
Having heard these words of Brahmā, he said to him, "O dear one,
O Grandfather, you do not know the sequence of the Chinese customs."
These people indeed constantly conquer through the great vidyā Ugratārā;
devoted to the Chinese tradition, they worship her alone.
All these practitioners are indeed great Kaulas of noble intent;
they have all attained liberation while living, O Goddess, being solely devoted to you.
By refraining from violating another's wife and from the constant drinking of intoxicants,
one obtains the highest fruit, which is even greater than that of the horse sacrifice (Aśvamedha).
"O Grandfather, censuring these [women] out of delusion, you have committed a great sin; go far away from here and do not touch me."
Thus, having released his vow, the Grandfather Brahmā, beholding that light,
was filled with supreme wonder, his mind overcome by doubt.
"What is this that has been proclaimed by Śambhu, which stands outside the conduct prescribed by the Vedas?"— thus reflecting, the Lotus-born One observed a vow of silence.
Then, having reached Vaikuṇṭha, he approached the supreme lord Śrī Viṣṇu and,
with palms joined in reverence, spoke all this as follows.
O God of gods, O Mahāviṣṇu, the cause of the existence of the world,
cut through my great doubt that resides within my mind, O Lord.
There is no one other than you who can sever this doubt;
it was for this very reason that I traveled to the Dāruvana forest from my wanderings among the sacred fords.
There, all the hosts of sages were intent on violating the wives of others;
their eyes were perpetually rolling from the consumption of intoxicating liquor.
Indeed, they were all shameless, taking pleasure with the wives of others;
having seen those of such wicked conduct, [he went] to the dweller of Kailāsa.
I told all of that to Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion;
then that Maheśvara praised even the sages of sinful conduct.
Filled with supreme faith, he addressed them again and again, saying: "Those noble ones are indeed liberated while living, men of great magnanimity."
Having censured those great sinners, they went far away from here;
therefore, O Lord of the Universe, filled with wonder, I have come to you.
"Cut asunder this doubt of mine, if you indeed possess compassion.
Thus addressed by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Lord and Master of all, [replied].
Endowed with supreme devotion, he bowed down to those sages and spoke these words,
consisting of the knowledge of reality, to the Creator:
In the Dāruvana forest, you saw those sages who are the grandfathers;
they are all excellent practitioners worshipping Tārā.
Those who violate the wives of others and constantly consume intoxicants shall attain liberation through the grace of the Bhagavatī.
Relying upon the conduct of China, all those high-minded sages,
who consist of the knowledge of reality, wander upon the surface of the earth.
Go quickly to that very place and propitiate them, O Lotus-born One;
when they have been individually appeased, even your status as Brahmā will be restored.
That which was spoken by Mahādeva is undoubtedly true for me;
whoever reviles other practitioners without having touched [the truth] of us both.
The illustrious Śiva said:
Then, having bowed to Viṣṇu, that Parameṣṭhin, filled with haste,
went to the Dāruvana forest and prostrated before all the lords of sages.
He praised them with supreme devotion through various hymns;
having obtained their grace, he became one who had fulfilled his purpose.
72b) The Goddess said:
O Maheśvara, tell me what Vasiṣṭha did thereafter— whether he practiced the Mahācīna-krama-ācāra or quickly [attained] the state of a Buddha and so forth.
The illustrious Śiva said:
Then, following the practice of the Mahācīna-krama, he— whose intellect and other faculties were likewise [perfected]—
reached Nīlācala, becoming fully devoted to the Kula-ācāra.
Then the sage, through his power, transformed the young woman Akṣamālā into a Cāṇḍālī; while reciting [the mantra], he brought this Tārā, the bestower of liberation, to perfection.
Intoxicated by the drinking of wine, and reeling with the intoxication of liquor,

Being free from sin and other defects, he becomes directly composed of Brahman;
having become identical with Sadāśiva, he should perform the five mudrās and so forth. || 59 ||
He who consists entirely of Brahman is not tainted by defects; nor is anyone here affected by delusion, passion, or greed. (60)
But for those practitioners who violate [the rules], it will certainly lead to rebirth in hell;
that which is called "samaya" (the time-limit) was previously indicated by me as the duration of my arrival. (61)
I shall now declare that for the purpose of recitation; listen, O beautiful one!
There are three times: morning, midday, and the third, which is dusk.
The first watch of the night and the fourth are proclaimed [as the times for worship];
the fifth is midnight; thus the five times (pañcakāla) are proclaimed. || 63 ||
The time at the beginning of the first watch of the day is declared the first;
the time in the middle of the day is proclaimed the second. (64)
When the sun has set and night has arrived, that time which follows midnight until the Brāhma-muhūrta is the third [period]. (66)

That time which is known as the sixth, difficult to obtain even for the gods, is used for pacification (śānti), ritual action (karma), subjugation (vaśya), immobilization (staṃbhana), and likewise for causing enmity (dveṣaka). || 67 ||
O beloved, hear now of the six rites: eradication and killing.
The first period is for the purpose of pacification; likewise, the middle one is for causing hatred. 68. 79a)

The third is declared for immobilization (staṃbhanam), the fourth for the rite of subjugation (vaśakarma), the fifth for eradication (uccāṭanam), and the sixth for the rite of killing (māraṇakarma). || 69 ||

The lotus posture (padmāsana) is prescribed for the svastika rite, and likewise the vikaṭa for the rite of hatred; one should know the cock posture (kukkuṭa) for the rite of immobilization, and the vajra for the rite of subjugation.
The knowledge for killing is auspicious; thus, six types of subjugation are proclaimed.
Thus ends the hymn to the Samayas.

Water is declared for the rite of pacification (śāntika), and fire is proclaimed for subjugation (vaśya); earth is to be known for paralyzing (staṃbhana), and likewise space for causing enmity (dveṣaṇa).
Vāyu is declared for the rite of eradication (uccāṭana), while Agni is considered suitable for the rite of killing (māraṇa);
whichever element [is required], O Goddess, that [mantra] should be given together with its corresponding maṇḍala.
For the purpose of performing those respective rites, one with a sharpened mind,
having first placed the seed-syllable of the Moon (Śītāṃśu) in the first [square], [places it] in the second.
The seed-syllable of the earth is the third, and the fourth is the seed-syllable of space;
the fifth is the seed-syllable of air, while the seed-syllable of fire is used for killing.
Thus has the time for the breaking of the convention been previously explained;
now, furthermore, I shall proclaim the fruit of the oral tradition (āmnāya). || 75 ||
The entire tradition (sarvāmnāya) was born at that time when the Lord Sadāśiva first stood in the eastern direction; he is proclaimed as the conduct (ācāra). || 76 ||
Thus the Southern Tradition is situated in the southern direction;
thus the Western Tradition is situated in the western direction. || 77 ||
Thus is the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya), situated in the northern direction;
it is that which was proclaimed to you in my presence, wherein the Goddess’s face is turned upward.
This is declared as the Upper Tradition (Ūrdhvāmnāya), difficult even for the gods to attain;
it was taught, O Goddess Girijā, my beloved, when [the world] was turned face downwards. 79.
O fair-faced one, it is truly, truly said that there are six Āmnāyas; and the one called Autpattikakrama is declared to be the sixth Āmnāya. (80)
In whichever group each respective deity is proclaimed, I shall declare those very deities for the benefit of practitioners. (81)
Śrīvidyā along with her divisions, Vālā, Tripurā, Bhuvaneśvarī, and Annapūrṇā are proclaimed in the Pūrvāmnāya. (82)
Vasini, the goddess Vagalā, who bestows fruit through Tvarita,
the slayer of the demon Mahiṣāsura, and Mahālakṣmī, who is Dakṣiṇā;
79b) In which [I] shall proclaim the deities for the benefit of practitioners. 83.
Śrīvidyā along with her divisions, Bālā, Tripurā, Bhuvaneśī, and Annapūrṇā—these are proclaimed in all the Āmnāyas. (84)
Mahāsarasvatī, the Vidyā, as well as Vāgvādinī, Pratyaṅgirā, and Bhavānī are the deities of the Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya). || 85 ||
Kālikā is considered to be accompanied by her divisions, as is Tārā with her various forms; likewise, Mātaṅgī, Bhairavī, Chinnā, and Dhūmāvatī are recognized.
The Uttarāmnāya is said to bestow the fruits of swift action;
all the deities, together with their various divisions, have been proclaimed therein. (87)
The mantra known as the twenty-two-syllabled one, belonging to the tradition of the South (Dakṣiṇāmnāya), is the supreme Prāsāda mantra, proclaimed for the sake of the upper half.
The Nāga-śakti and other vidyās are proclaimed in the lower tradition (adhomnāya);
however, in the upper tradition (ūrdhvāmnāya), both above and below, there is that which bestows liberation alone.
The various traditions have been proclaimed for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa;
by consuming [the substance] according to the prescribed rule, one shall obtain the fruit.
O beautiful one, having established this for the sake of the ritual procedure of all traditions,
by means of which one quickly attains the supreme mass of fruits of both [the paths].
O Goddess of the Gods, he who is proclaimed in all the traditions as the bestower of the fruits of the six rites, bestows their fruit swiftly in the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya). 92.
The hero, having bathed and wearing white garments, as well as she who wears pure attire, were both constantly devoted to the worship of the gods during the day. (93)
If all materials and so forth are prepared at night according to the rules, with the best available means and according to one's capacity, it shall yield all fruits. || 94 ||
Listen as I declare the rosaries for all [practitioners] of the Eastern Tradition and others;
by chanting with which one quickly obtains results that are very difficult even for the gods to attain. (95)
Akṣamālā is first of all the embodiment of the cause that is Mātṛkā;
furthermore, she consists of the liberated (mukta) and bestows the fruit of liberation.

A garland of all kinds of jewels brings about every accomplishment; a garland of coral brings all kingdoms under one's control and bestows the fruits of all undertakings for the purpose of subjugation. 80a) 96.
A garland fashioned from rubies bestows the fruit of universal sovereignty;
a garland made of putrajīvaka seeds grants fortune and knowledge. (97)
A rosary made of lotus seeds bestows fame and fortune;
a rosary made of gold, silver, or crystal grants all desires.
A rosary made of red sandalwood inevitably bestows enjoyments;
a rosary fashioned from rudrākṣa beads grants the fruit of all desires. (99)

For the sake of worshipping the entire garland, having smeared it with sandalwood paste and other substances, one should take recourse to it and recite the vidyā; thus one attains the fruit as described. (100)
These auspicious garlands are honored in the five Āmnāyas;
O Girijā, I shall now tell you of that garland which belongs to the Uttara-āmnāya.
The rosary made of Atharvan beads is considered the most excellent of all,
while that made of great conch shells bestows the fruits of one's desired objects.
A rosary fashioned from crystal, or produced from the fruit of the rudrākṣa,
is considered to grant its fruits when made from materials ranging from gold to precious gems.
Likewise, a garland of guñjā seeds should be made, which bestows the fruits of one's desires;
so too one made from small udumbara fruits. (104)
O Goddess of the gods, a man should perform the *mālā* [mantra] in this manner according to the prescribed rule.
Now, I shall explain the supreme procedure for the *yantra*. (105)
For copper, it is twelve times for six years;
for gold, it is six times; and for a great conch-shell, it is a thousandfold.
In the case of gold and crystal, there is no fixed number of years;
for the sake of swiftly accomplishing the task, one should install [the image] upon a crystal.

Having drawn [the diagram] according to the prescribed rule and always performing the worship as described, the practitioner of mantra obtains his desired object; otherwise, he does not obtain the fruit.
I shall describe the seats; listen, O Goddess, as I speak.
For the purpose of subjugation, one uses a ram skin, and for attraction, a tiger skin. (109)
O Goddess, for pacification, a deer skin is recommended; for liberations, a tiger skin; for paralyzing, a cow hide; and for paralyzing as well, the hide of a bull.
For the purpose of eradication, one should use the skin of a camel; for causing hatred, the skin of a dog;
and for killing, one should know it to be the skin of a buffalo—or one may proceed according to the sequence previously specified.
O Goddess, likewise, a seat made of cloth or silk,
a woolen seat, a blanket, and so forth, when well-honored, grants all desires and is effective for every ritual action.
O Beloved, it pacifies suffering and poverty; O Goddess, the seat made of the wood of the *vidyā* tree, when fashioned from gold or other materials and colored red, increases great good fortune.
Listen, O Goddess, specifically to the seat of the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya), by which one quickly obtains merit and even the fruit that is very difficult to attain. || 114 ||
O fortunate one, there is likewise the seat of the skull with its latent impressions (savāsana), as well as the seat of the new moon (darśāsana) and the seat of sexual union (maithunāsana). || 115 ||
And even when sexual intercourse has been performed, it bestows the fruit of one's desired object. || 116 ||
O Goddess of the Gods, the places for recitation and so forth, as well as those sacred sites of accomplishment (siddhitīrtha),
the seats of accomplishment (siddhipīṭha), and the fields of accomplishment (siddhikṣetra) are likewise found on mountains and in temples.
One should perform it at a banyan tree, under a universal tree (viśvavṛkṣa), or in a grove of plantain trees; or on the bank of a river and the like, or in a cave on a mountain peak.
Listen, O Goddess, specifically for the sake of the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya):
having gone to a prostitute’s house or to a cremation ground, one should engage in sexual union. || 119 ||
Then, O Goddess, by performing the recitation and other rites, one easily attains the fruit;
or else, he who is devoted may perform them at night in his own home. (120)
He attains the entire fruit, freed from anxiety and fear;
now, therefore, I shall describe the worship of Bhaga in brief.
With that very mantra which the practitioner constantly recites from the presence of his guru, the mantrin performs the worship of the Bhaga.
Then, one should contemplate her in the form of Brahman within the center of the *bhaga*;
having become Śiva, one should remember [her] in the body and meditate upon oneself as such. 123.
One should know that Śakti is identical with that Vidyā; having truly attained her, one should engage in sexual union. O Goddess, he who acts as prescribed attains the supreme state.
O fair-faced goddess, those fabricated mantras which have been taught must be understood, O Goddess, as they truly are in all tantras; this is certain. 81a) 125.
Some are proclaimed as mantras, while others are celebrated as vidyās.
Mantras whose presiding deities are male are called mantras, whereas those whose names are feminine are known as vidyās. || 126 ||
All these mantras declared [in this context] are neuter;
those ending in *huṃ* and *phaṭ* are male, while those ending in *svāhā* are considered female. (127)
The neuter [mantras] should end with "namaḥ" and are further divided into three types according to their genus:
Granthana, Vidarbha, Saṃpuṭa, and likewise Rodhana. (128)
Some say that yoga is fruitful;
the syllables of the names are likewise interspersed within the mantras according to the rule for auspicious rites. (129)
One should perform what is called "tying" (granthana), which is praised in rites for pacification (śānti).
One should write the syllables of the name of the person to be protected (sādhya) situated between two syllables of the mantra. || 130 ||
The *vidarbha* (enveloping) is praised for the rite of subjugation (*vaśyakarman*);
it is known as "encapsulation" (*saṃpuṭa*) when the name is placed at both the beginning and the end of the mantra. || 131 ||

O Goddess, if it is performed as prescribed, this is praised for the purpose of immobilization (staṃbhanam). It is considered that the mantra should be inserted at the beginning, the end, and the middle of the name. || 132 ||
This is declared to be the most excellent among the rites for causing enmity;
in the rite of eradication (uccāṭana), it is held that the name should be placed at the end of the mantra.
Before the name, there shall be the mantra; this is considered the "sprout" (pallava) in the rite of killing (māraṇa).
It has come from the mouth of Śiva and gone into the mouth of Girijā.
By him, O fair-faced one, the Āgamas and Tantras were spoken;
and the Pāṇika scriptures of the Āgama were also spoken.
O beautiful one, those various worldly customs are being proclaimed;
and that conduct which was described by her has been practiced upon the earth. (136)
By the name of that conduct, it is proclaimed as *kulācāra*;
that which is devoid of the five seals (*pañcamudrā*) and so forth is designated as *dakṣiṇācāra*. (137)
O Goddess of the gods, there are various mantras, distinct Yāmalas, and all other [texts], as well as the heart-essences (hṛdaya) of all mantras. (138)
I shall speak in brief; listen, O Goddess, as I speak.
"O beautiful one, there are sixty-four tantras and eight yāmalas; O lady of auspicious countenance, there are also three amaras—these I shall describe. (139)
O Goddess, many tantras have been revealed by me previously;
now I shall speak further of the Yāmalas and likewise the Amarās.
The *Yāmalas* of Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and Śiva are each distinct;
likewise, those of Śakti and Gaṇapati are each distinct in the month of Kārtika. (141)
O fair-faced one, those belonging to the Sun and the Moon have also been declared;
likewise, the Uḍḍīśaḍāmara and the Bhūtaḍāmara.
O Pārvatī, O fair-faced one, how shall I today proclaim the Śaktiḍāmaraka, the Amaraṇi, and the other Tantras? 143.
Sixty-four tantras are renowned in the Vāmakeśvara;
therefore, the Kula conduct has not been mentioned in those tantras—O Guru, listen! (144)
Skilled in the traditional scriptures and conduct, the best among the upholders of all treatises, well-attired, dexterous, truthful in speech, and pleasant of address. (145)
Thus, one endowed with these characteristics is considered a teacher according to the tradition;
as for the disciple, he should always be possessed of virtues and devoted to the teacher.
He was devoted to righteous deeds and the like, dedicated to his guru and the mantra;
he was an ocean of truth toward his guru and the mantra, and intent upon the worship of the deity. (147)
Having fixed his mind upon the path indicated by the Guru, the noble-minded disciple, endowed with such characteristics, is indeed a discerning one.
Free from deceit, censure, and the like, and devoid of laziness and other such faults; endowed with the conduct of the observances (samaya), wealthy, and possessing three wives. || 149 ||
Śrī Sadāśiva said: 1.
I shall now explain the materials for worship so that the desires of the worshipper may be fulfilled;
for by knowing the mantra correctly, one obtains the full fruit of worship even without [other] ritual requirements. 150.
Liquor, meat, fish, parched grain, and sexual union—
these five things beginning with the letter 'ma,' O auspicious lady, are for the sake of the ritual acts along with their constituent parts.

O Goddess, just as that liquor which is described in all the mantras is difficult to obtain on earth, so too may there be a sacred ford (tīrtha) by that name, which is difficult to attain through knowledge. 152.
O Goddess, the flesh of animals fit for consumption has been ordained;
and through the mantra of the Goddess, its supreme accomplishment is declared according to the prescribed rule. 153.
O fair-faced one, those fish which have been mentioned regarding the consumption of meat have been declared by me in secret to be the fish that bestow spiritual accomplishment (siddhi). (154)
They place jaggery and other such items inside [the vessel] to increase its luster;
they call that the *mudrā*, as do roasted chickpeas and the like. (155)
O Goddess, that which is called Yāroṭikā and Polikā is declared auspicious in times of fear;
its nameless form, O Goddess, bestows liberation through mudrā.
O Dear One, O Goddess, that which occurs as sexual union through the joining of the linga with the bhaga is proclaimed by the name of the fifth [tattva]. || 157 ||
The first occurs with liquor, and the second also with meat;
the third would be with fish, and the fourth is the name of the mudrā. 158.
In the fifth [vow], sexual intercourse is known; these five are remembered by that name.
O fair-faced one, the names of the five [elements] consist of the five syllables beginning with the letter 'a'. (159)
The five rare syllables "ma" belong to the first, second, third, fourth, and likewise the fifth deity. (160)
O Goddess, O beloved, my life-force resides in all five [syllables].
O Goddess, without the fifth, one would chant the Caṇḍī-mantra in vain. (161)
If one creates delusion regarding all aspects, O beloved, how can there be accomplishment for him, O Goddess? How can he recite the Śakti-mantra? (162)
O Goddess, without the fifth, how can there be enjoyment and liberation?
O Goddess, without the fifth, how can [the practice] be fruit-bearing? || 163 ||
O Goddess, when Nanda is certainly present without the fifth [element], that is liberation for the wise; for those lacking it, it is a sin. (164)
The supreme bliss is Brahman, which indicates the bliss of the letter 'A';
likewise, O Goddess, it is specifically proclaimed as the fifth.
There is merit in the remembrance of Bhaga, likewise in the sight of Bhaga;
there is merit in the worship of Bhaga, and likewise in the fifth [act] toward Bhaga. || 166 ||
O Goddess, that bliss which arises in the fifth state of Bhaga is not attained through recitations, burnt offerings, gifts, or asceticism. (82b) 167.
O Goddess, the merit that arises from performing the fifth [rite] is such that, O Goddess, even the sight of ten million sacred fords (tīrthas) is not equal to that merit. || 168 ||
Recitation, fire-offerings, as well as giving, initiation, yoga, and other such conceptual practices,
do not equal even a sixteenth part of one who has observed the fifth meal (the fast).
O beloved, from the age of thirteen onwards, specifically for one who has not yet given birth, she becomes eligible for the fifth [initiation] up until the twenty-fifth year.
O Maheśvarī, whether she has not yet given birth or has already given birth, a woman who has recently delivered must certainly perform the fifth [rite], even if she possesses only limited capacity.
O Goddess, whatever worship and other rites one performs when the fifth [digit] has been completed, one shall obtain imperishable merit; there is no need for deliberation on this point. || 172 ||
There, O beautiful one, he should satisfy the guru with various ornaments, garments, and other such things, as well as with wealth, whether it be his wife or his daughter who serves him by day.
The fifth meaning is according to Śakti; one should perform the fifth [rite] within her, and one should also perform her hymn of praise—listen specifically, O beloved. (174)
Listen now to the supreme secret regarding the bathing of the deities with substances, ornaments, garments, unguents, and so forth. (175)
O Goddess, when this bath has been performed, the deities become well-pleased;
having practiced the fifth among the five makāras at night, it is supreme. (176)
Whatever substance one should diligently take from the centers of her vulva,
that should be known as the water born of the *kuṇḍa*, which bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Through the conjunction of good fortune, one obtains that which is difficult even for the gods to attain;
having poured a little water into it, one should hold it in copper vessels. || 178 ||
The deity becomes well-pleased by the mere bathing with that substance. As for women, it is at the age when the first menses occurs. (179)
O auspicious one, quickly take this flower called Svayambhū, which is difficult even for Brahmā and others to obtain, for the pleasure of the deities.
O Goddess, if by the power of fortune one obtains this flower,
then one should perform the supreme bath for one's own deities.
The practitioner of mantra obtains his desire; this is the truth, the absolute truth, O fair-faced one.
Having received the mantra from his own guru, he should perform the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa). 83a) 182.
Then, one should have the fifth [rite] performed either upon the body of the Śakti or upon one's own body;
thereafter, one should perform recitation (japa) and other rites, and thus obtains imperishable fruit. || 183 ||
This secret has been told for the purpose of bathing the deity;
this secret is proclaimed in the tantras of the six traditions (ṣaḍāmnāya). || 184 ||
One should especially perform [this] within the mantras of the Uttarāmnāya;
O Dear One, for women whose husbands are living, one should cause the fifth [initiation] to be performed.
Whatever substance belongs to her vulva is said to be produced from the kuṇḍa;
if, upon the death of her husband, one should cause women to perform the fifth [rite]. (186)
Whatever substance belongs to her vulva is produced from a cow and is dead;
listen, O beautiful one, regarding the substances produced from the *kuṇḍa* and the *goḷa* in their absence.
How should one perform the ritual bath for the sake of pleasing the deity?
Having quickly and diligently taken [water] from any meritorious tree whatsoever, [one should proceed]. (188)
Among those, two should be grasped with the hands and one with the mind;
then, a person should perform the fifth of both according to the prescribed rule.
Then, one should sprinkle water that has been rubbed with red sandalwood;
with that water, one should perform the supreme bathing of the deity. || 190 ||
O fair-faced one, he obtains his desired fruit; this is the truth, the absolute truth.
[He obtains] all the flowers of the creepers and whatever flowers belong to the trees. (191)
O auspicious lady, one should offer all those flowers that grow among every kind of medicinal herb to the deities.
In all traditions, offerings devoid of *tulasī* are not authorized;
likewise, the *aparājitā* flower and whatever other pair of flowers there may be [are also prohibited]. (193)
Whatever merit belongs to the karavīra flower, whatever the budhvajīvaka flower, the lotus flower, and the flower of the five-fold [group]. || 194 ||
And especially among all flowers, O beautiful one, bilva leaves are most suitable for the purpose of worship on the day of Śukla-pakṣa. (195)
Now, I shall proclaim the supreme sacred seat (pīṭha) for the purpose of recitation:
Pūrṇagiri is suitable for the Kṛta age, and that known as Upāna for the Tretā age. (196)
In the Dvāpara age, it was Jālandhara; in the Kali age, it is Kāmapīṭha.
O auspicious one, those four seats which exist within the bodies of Śaktis [are these]. (197)
I shall describe those four, which are more secret than the secret;
Śakti is the entire body, while Pīṭha is considered to be Pūrṇagiri. (198)
O fortunate one, her head has been described by me as Uḍyāna; her two breasts are to be known as Jālandhara, and her vulva is remembered as Kāmapīṭha. || 199 ||
Among all [seats], that which is the seat of desire (kāmapīṭha) is difficult even for the gods to attain;
O Dear One, whatever mantra one recites while stationed upon those seats, [that very mantra becomes effective]. 200.
He obtains that fruit; the deity becomes well-pleased.
He obtains the ultimate fruit of all; the deity becomes well-pleased. || 201 ||
And listen, O beloved, to the offering of oblations for all the deities.
By means of which, having made it easy to obtain, the practitioner always, at the time of his own meal, attains the supreme fruit as desired through the root mantra. (202)
O Dear One, one should first offer the oblation before eating;
then, O Goddess, being pure and absorbed in that, one rejoices. (203)
One should carefully lift up the offering and then place it in a secluded spot;
having placed the offering there, one may then enjoy oneself as one pleases.
O Goddess of the gods, the traditions of the Uttarāmnāya are proclaimed as those of Mātaṅgī;
in that tradition, the offering (bali) is made at the end of the meal even without the performance of the ritual rinsing (ācamana). || 205 ||
O auspicious lady, having diligently offered the bali-oblation with the root mantra,
and having performed some recitation (japa) and so forth, one should then perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and other rites.
Furthermore, having diligently offered the bali-oblation to all of them at night, one should perform it according to the prescribed rule;
thus one enjoys the fruit as described. || 207 ||
And the offering (bali) is of various kinds, O Goddesses: sattvic as well as rājasic.
That which is called the sattvic bali is devoid of meat, blood, and the like. || 208 ||
O Dear One, that which is joined with flesh, blood, and so forth is declared to be *rājasa*.
Practitioners are said to be of three kinds: *sāttvika*, *rājasa*, and *tāmasa*. (209)
And likewise, O Goddess, I shall describe the characteristics of those who are characterized by tamas.
One should diligently perform the offering of oblations and other such rites, which are characterized by sattva, as a constant duty.

O lady of auspicious countenance, one who is always endowed with the qualities of the *rājasa* [nature] performs *rājasa* offerings such as the *bali* sacrifice, being accompanied by those of a *rājasa* disposition and fine attire. (212)
O beloved, those who are dominated by tamas are joined with qualities such as anger and the like;
O beautiful one, they have no faith in offerings, worship, and other such rites.
O Goddess, a practitioner does not succeed merely by reciting hymns or even by my name alone;
therefore, O beautiful one, I shall now proclaim my mantras.
Those mantras of mine which are here well-known by their very nature, as well as the great mantra called Aghora, which delivers one from calamity; || 215 ||
Likewise, O Goddess, [worship] Cintāmaṇi, as well as Mṛtyuñjayavara; O fortunate one, [worship] Caṇḍovara, Ardhanārī, and Naṭeśvara. || 216 ||
O Goddess of gods, whatever mantras of mine exist in various tantras,
O auspicious lady, they should always be understood as being within the six traditions (ṣaḍāmnāya).

O Goddess, by reciting with the left-hand practice (vāmācāra), one shall obtain the fruit; or by reciting through the yoga of the right-hand practice (dakṣiṇācāra), one shall obtain the fruit. || 218 ||
O auspicious one, whatever mantras belong to me, even those [associated with] poison,
bestow their fruit quickly when performed according to the procedure of all the Āgamas.
O beloved Goddess, the mantras that remove various sins are like wish-fulfilling cows;
O Goddess, whatever mantra a hero recites with his mind fixed upon it, [he attains its fruit]. (220)
Having attained each respective state, a person obtains its corresponding fruit;
O Goddess of gods, such are your mantras and those which are mine.
Whatever things are well-known, O Goddess, those very same ones were proclaimed by the Self-Existent One as the four Vedas. || 222 ||

Having thoroughly investigated the deities who have been perfectly accomplished since beginningless time, they should be understood according to their distinctions within the various traditions of the revealed scriptures (śrutāmnāya). || 223 ||
Thus have the six Āmnāyas been declared by me to you in their presence;
that Āmnāya is to be known from the Śruti, and the Śruti is obtained from the Veda.
Therefore, O Girijā, you too must keep this secret as you would your own birth.
Now, from this point forward, I shall proclaim the supreme and auspicious secret.
When the practitioner has many mantras due to the conjunction of fate, with whom among these—such as virtuous people and others—should he perform the recitation? (226)
One should constantly and with effort pay homage to all the gods; furthermore, one should perform recitation and other rites for whichever deity the mind is inclined toward. (227)
O beautiful one, if a practitioner, having received a mantra from his guru, abandons it due to wicked conduct, negligence, or even laziness; || 228 ||

the second belongs to the fifth [consonant] and is known by the fifth vowel.
O Goddess of the gods, the third syllable is excellent and joined with the visarga;
O Mistress of the gods, it is endowed with the essence of Sūrya, possessed of a vowel, and joined with the bindu.
O Brahmin, one should place the vowel in the fourth [syllable] and the consonant in the sixth;
joined with the syllable *oṃ* and likewise with a salutation, one should perform the placement (*vinyāsa*).
This eight-syllable mantra bestows all spiritual accomplishments.
Oṃ, homage to the King of Elephants, who is red and tawny! Stop the blood of women! Mudga 2! Laka 2!
Stake it down 2! Cili 2! Svāhā! This is the mantra for warding off excessive menstruation in women.
Thus ends the second ritual procedure for the adorned owl. May there be auspiciousness.
